images.title: Three half rotis
images.purpose: Show that three halves of a roti make one whole roti and one half more: 3/2 = 1 + 1/2.
images.composition: One whole roti made of two halves on the left, a plus sign, and one half roti on the right, with one equation centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: one round roti made of exactly 2 equal half pieces fitted together along a visible straight cut, both halves filled teal #0072B2. Centre: a plain plus sign. Right: exactly 1 half roti of the same size as each left half, filled amber #E69F00. Below, centred: one line of equation text. Exactly 3 half pieces in all, all exactly the same size.

images.takeaway: Three halves is one whole and one half more.
images.description: Two teal half rotis fit into one whole roti labelled 1/2 + 1/2 = 1, plus one amber half labelled 1/2; below, 3/2 = 1 + 1/2.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the half pieces and say how many whole rotis they can make.

image_decisions.why: Pairing halves into a whole roti is a picture idea that one clean image carries.
